species.name: Corscout
species.description: Young birds trained by the ancient armies as messengers. Their light armor allows them to fly swiftly between outposts. The red trim on their armor designates them as military couriers.

species.name: Centurvus
species.description: Bearing the marks of rank on its armor, Centurvus command small flocks of Corscout. Their distinctive cry can be heard coordinating aerial formations above ancient battlefields.

species.name: Praetorvus
species.description: Elite guardians of the ancient empire, Praetorvus were feared for their combination of military might and political influence. Their purple-trimmed armor marked them as extensions of imperial authority.

species.name: Growlithe
species.description: These wild canines are skilled hunters that roam the grasslands in small packs. Unlike other regions' variants, Shiman Growlithe have developed more powerful jaws and a keen sense for tracking wounded prey. They've been observed caching their kills in hidden locations, returning to feed multiple times.

species.name: Arcanine
species.description: A fearsome predator that claims vast territories in both forests and grasslands. Their fire sacs have evolved to produce short, intense bursts of flame that can quickly incapacitate prey. They're known to share their kills with their pack, and ancient folklore speaks of them leaving food for travelers lost in their territory.

species.name: Growlarc
species.description: These electric hunters generate static charges in their fur that can paralyze small prey. Their hunting technique involves short bursts of incredible speed, powered by electrical discharges through their leg muscles. Though rare, they can sometimes be spotted at dawn, feeding on prey taken during night hunts.

species.name: Sparcanine
species.description: A powerful predator among Shiman's electric-types, Sparcanine's hunting prowess is legendary. They can accurately sense prey's bioelectric signatures from great distances. When they make a kill, they've been observed using electrical charges to preserve their food, returning to feed over several days. Despite their fearsome reputation, they rarely attack humans who respect their territory.

species.name: Jiehtanas
species.description: Driftlands oral traditions describe Jiehtanas as an ancient guardian that watches the stars for signs of danger. Its true nature and motives are unknown to outside scholars, and the northern peoples share little about it with outsiders.

species.name: Tempus
species.description: Local legends warn travelers not to sleep near ancient ruins, as Tempus packs are known to shepherd unprotected minds into the Sea of Dreams. The markings in their fur shift like starlight on water.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level up near temporal anomaly, or during lunar phase event

species.name: Chronus
species.description: Each of its multiple tails exists in a different moment in time. When it howls, some claim to hear echoes of their past and glimpses of possible futures.

species.name: Scrabshell
species.description: This industrious Pokémon scuttles along harbor floors, consuming debris and waste. Its shell is partially made from reclaimed materials, which it constantly upgrades and reinforces. Colonies of Scrabshell are considered essential for maintaining clean waterways, and they're often seen working in teams to break down larger pieces of refuse.

species.name: Reclaimant
species.description: The evolved form of Scrabshell has developed specialized chambers in its shell for processing different types of waste. It can extract and purify useful materials from almost anything it consumes. Harbor authorities often track Reclaimant movements to identify areas needing cleanup, as these Pokémon instinctively gather where pollution is highest.

species.name: Purifax
species.description: This custodian of harbor waters can purify large volumes of water through its advanced filtration system. Ancient texts speak of Purifax appearing in polluted ports to restore life to dying waters. The sacred waters around the Abyss Arena are said to be maintained by a particularly old specimen.

species.name: Meowser
species.description: A stealthy urban hunter specializing in controlling Swarmy populations. Its whiskers can detect vibrations through walls, allowing it to track prey inside buildings. Shop owners often leave bowls of milk out to attract these helpful Pokémon to their establishments.

species.name: Preowlith
species.description: Evolved from Meowser, this proud hunter is highly territorial but can be befriended by those who earn its trust. It's known for its ability to organize other Meowser into coordinated hunting groups. Many Market Quarter shops have a resident Preowlith that's been with the family for generations.

species.name: Harbeak
species.description: This keen-eyed seabird has an uncanny ability to sense approaching storms. It communicates weather changes through distinct patterns of calls, which experienced sailors have learned to interpret. Harbeak often nest in harbor towers where they can survey wide areas.

species.name: Storican
species.description: The evolved form of Harbeak develops powerful psychic abilities that allow it to detect weather patterns days in advance. They work in pairs to patrol harbor airways, using telepathic bonds to coordinate their weather monitoring. The Harbor Master's office maintains a special roost for these valuable Pokémon.

species.name: Morbit
species.description: These diligent Pokémon are natural engineers, constantly working to maintain canal walls and waterways. They use their special sense for water flow to identify and repair weaknesses before they become problems. Morbit families pass down knowledge of their canal sections through generations.

species.name: Darbit
species.description: The evolved form of Morbit has an almost architectural understanding of water flow dynamics. They can reshape entire sections of canal to improve water flow, and their work is so precise that city planners often study their modifications. Some ancient canals show signs of being initially designed by Darbit.

species.name: Knighturn
species.description: This mysterious Pokémon appears as an animated suit of armor carrying an eternally burning lantern. They patrol historic districts at night, their lanterns glowing with an otherworldly light that is said to reveal hidden truths. Some believe they are the spirits of ancient city guards still maintaining their watch.

species.name: Nacleaf
species.description: Found wherever fresh water meets the sea, this adaptable plant Pokémon grows in dense clusters along coastlines. Its specialized leaves can process both fresh and salt water, making it vital to coastal ecosystems. Young shoots are sometimes used in cooking for their salty flavor.

species.name: Crystalga
species.description: Crystalga creates crystalline structures that serve as nurseries for small Water-type Pokémon. Most abundant in the calm waters of Florinex Bay, though also found along most of Shima's eastern coast. Their growth patterns are studied by the region's marine researchers.

species.name: Silkonat
species.description: Trees that have been infested with Silkonat become completely covered in a silky substance, making them stand out. They prefer making their homes in the forest, in secluded areas with few predators.

species.name: Silkomoth
species.description: These small moths have adapted to life in Shiman settlements, from the largest cities to remote villages. They play a crucial role in breaking down organic waste and fabric debris. Particularly common in the textile districts of Sylvaris and the Federation.

species.name: Weavoth
species.description: Known for their softly glowing wing patterns, Weavoth are especially active during festivals and full moons. Large populations can be found in the older cities of the Federation, with notable variations in pattern and color between regions.

species.name: Mergato
species.description: Distinguished by its sleek gray and white coat and distinctive whiskers, Mergato displays an almost supernatural sense of balance, able to traverse ship rigging with ease. The markings around its neck resemble a sailor's collar, leading to myths that they are the spirits of lost seafarers. Though fully capable of swimming when needed, these elegant felines prefer to stay above the waterline, using their keen eyes to spot approaching storms or schools of fish from their high perches in the ship's rigging.

species.name: Merchent
species.description: This seafaring evolution of Redent has developed vibrant red and blue markings that help it blend with both sunset-lit waters and ocean depths. Its thick mane and bushy tail have adapted to repel water while providing warmth in cold seas. Known for their proud demeanor, Merchent often stake out territory around busy ports where they hunt for fish and assert dominance over local water-type Pokémon despite not being one themselves.

species.name: Driftling
species.description: Found on calm waters throughout Shima's temperate regions, these Pokémon form colonies that help maintain water quality. They're especially common in the river systems of Montevera and the gentle waters of Florinex Bay.

species.name: Aquider
species.description: Aquider develops complex social behaviors and an acute sense for water conditions. Shiman sailors have long relied on their movement patterns to predict weather changes. They're particularly numerous in protected harbors and river mouths.

species.name: Mossling
species.description: These small Pokémon naturally bond with stone surfaces throughout Shima's temperate zones. They're essential to preserving both natural rock formations and ancient structures. Archaeologists particularly value their presence at historical sites.

species.name: Mossaic
species.description: The evolved form creates distinctive patterns that vary by region, with the oldest specimens found on ancient ruins and temples. Historians in Shima often use their patterns to help date stone structures. Some temples in Celestis maintain the same Mossaic colonies that have existed for centuries.

species.name: Buzzlet
species.description: This tiny Pokémon flits around forest ponds at dusk. The curl on its head glows softly to attract small prey, while its leaf-like wings help it blend in with foliage.

species.name: Mosqaegis
species.description: Its body has developed a natural armor. While it still retains its elegant appearance, it can now defend itself effectively against bigger predators while hunting.

species.name: Nectini
species.description: Primarily found in areas with abundant berry plants, particularly in the agricultural regions of Amalfara and Florinex. Also common in the wild berry groves of Libra Coast.

species.name: Dustwig
species.description: Found throughout the Aridune Desert and desert regions of Sylvaris, particularly around oases and areas with seasonal blooms. Also common near the Wandering Oases.

species.name: Blossomini
species.description: Its appearance can shift to mimic various flowers, but its natural form resembles a small rose or lily. The center of its flower form contains a face that can be either visible or hidden behind petals. Its body emits a faint, pleasant fragrance that changes with its mood.

species.name: Mushusk
species.description: Primarily found in damp forests, particularly in the densely wooded areas of Libra Coast and Florinex. They thrive in areas with heavy leaf litter and fallen logs, especially in older growth forests where dead wood accumulates.

species.name: Spectrout
species.description: Found in polluted waterways, particularly in urban areas and near industrial sites. Also common in natural water bodies with high organic waste content. Its skeleton is visible through its spectral flesh, and its fins seem to phase in and out of existence. Dark spots along its sides absorb toxins from the water, and its eyes glow with an eerie white light.

species.name: Moldite
species.description: Their color shifts based on the nutrients they're processing, ranging from pale green to deep purple. When forming colonies, they create intricate patterns that can span large areas. Particularly common in areas with extensive fungal networks.

species.name: Grazeep
species.description: Primarily found in highland pastures and rolling hills, particularly in the northern regions of the Shiman Federation. They are most common in Procello and the Rugitus Coast, where frequent storms help them build up their electrical charge.

species.name: Hoppit
species.description: Its fur changes color seasonally, from brown in summer to gray in winter. Its large ears can rotate independently to detect danger, and its powerful legs allow for quick escapes and impressive leaps.

species.name: Mounteer
species.description: Its thick, dual-layered coat changes seasonally, and its specialized hooves can grip almost any surface. The crystalline horns grow in geometric patterns that become more complex with age.

species.name: Lanfae
species.description: Lanfae were once thought to be animated artifacts from the ancient civilization. They gather near noble houses that possess old relics, drawn to the residual ether energy. Their bodies naturally form from steel exposed to concentrated fairy energy for centuries.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level up holding noble house artifact

species.name: Lumifae
species.description: Lumifae are deeply connected to the ancient noble houses. Their bodies contain metal believed to have been forged during the Age of Wonders. Some noble families claim these rare Pokémon once served as guardians of their ancestral artifacts.

species.name: Prankis
species.description: Prankis are known for harmless but elaborate pranks that never cause lasting harm. Noble children often keep them as playmates, as their presence is said to bring good fortune and laughter to a household. They can create small, convincing illusions to aid their mischief.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level up with high happiness after making at least 3 different people laugh.

species.name: Trixen
species.description: Trixen have been associated with noble houses for centuries, with some families even featuring them in their coat of arms. Though their pranks become more elaborate with evolution, they possess an innate sense of dignity that prevents causing true embarrassment. Their illusions can be so convincing that historical records sometimes mention them being mistaken for actual people.

species.name: Sylvix
species.description: Sylvix are born from the purest forest energy, appearing in areas where the boundary between our world and the fairy realm thins. They protect young plants and small forest creatures. Gardens tended by Sylvix flourish with unusual vigor and resist disease and pests.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level 5, long rest in a sacred forest location

species.name: Verdiane
species.description: Verdiane guard ancient forest groves with unwavering devotion. Their presence causes flowers to bloom out of season and trees to bear fruit year-round. Early Shiman settlers would leave offerings at forest edges to gain Verdiane's blessing for their farms and gardens.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level 15, successfully defending a forest from a significant threat

species.name: Sylvestra
species.description: Sylvestra are so rare that many believe them to be mere legends. Ancient texts describe them as guardians of sacred boundaries between worlds, and that forests protected by Sylvestra never wither, remaining vibrant even during the harshest winters. Some noble houses claim their ancestral grounds were blessed by these mystical beings centuries ago.

species.name: Faeling
species.description: Faeling are believed to be the result of dragon eggs exposed to fairy energy. Despite their dragon heritage, they're gentle creatures that prefer playing to fighting.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level up after helping establish peace between conflicting parties

species.name: Drairy
species.description: Throughout Shiman history, the appearance of a Drairy has heralded an era of peace. Some noble houses still display their shed scales as symbols of diplomatic prowess.

species.name: Kortier
species.description: Kortiers have been associated with noble houses since ancient times. They appear in gardens of grand estates, mimicking the mannerisms of their human counterparts with comical precision. Some historical texts suggest they once served as advisors to the ancient civilization's elite.

species.name: Noblier
species.description: Noblier are said to embody the ideal virtues of nobility. Ancient texts suggest they once served as advisors to emperors.

species.name: Aurette
species.description: Aurette are drawn to sources of light and warmth, particularly the ancestral flame of House Luminis. Ancient texts describe them dancing above the original Eternal Flame like living stars. They are capable of absorbing and redirecting light, sometimes creating dazzling displays to communicate with each other.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level 10 long exposure to Eternal Flame

species.name: Luminarch
species.description: Historical records from the ancient civilization depict them as guardians of sacred flames and keepers of celestial knowledge. House Luminis claims their Eternal Flame was once tended by these magnificent beings. When a Luminarch appears, those in its presence report feelings of profound hope and clarity.

species.name: Clingae
species.description: Clingae are believed to be the result of fae spirits inhabiting ancient metal objects. APEX hunters often seek them as companions for their reliable warning abilities. When danger approaches, Bellfae emit a distinctive chime that carries for miles. Some remote villages maintain special bell towers hoping to attract these protective Pokémon.

evolvesInto.requirement: Help protect others from danger at least three times

species.name: Chimae
species.description: Chimae are revered guardians that have protected communities for generations. Their chimes can be heard over vast distances, each tone conveying specific warnings about approaching threats. The oldest bells in Shiman cathedrals are said to have been modeled after these protective Pokémon.

species.name: Starcub
species.description: Starcub were once believed to be created from children's wishes upon stars. Their gentle presence has a calming effect on both people and Pokémon, making them popular companions for young trainers. Wild Pokémon rarely show aggression toward them, and even territorial species will often allow Starcub safe passage through their domains.

evolvesInto.requirement: Level up at night with high friendship

species.name: Stellursa
species.description: Stellursa are said to walk between dreams and reality. Their appearance is often linked to periods of peace and prosperity in historical records. Children who sleep near Stellursa report vivid, beautiful dreams and wake feeling refreshed even after just a short rest. Some astronomers believe these Pokémon can navigate by the stars with perfect accuracy, regardless of cloud cover.

species.name: Voltey
species.description: Often found practicing punches and kicks on trees near power lines that naturally attract electrical energy. The patterns on its fur glow brighter as it builds up power through exercise.

species.name: Dynape
species.description: The energy coursing through its enhanced muscles can be unleashed through its powerful strikes. When threatened, it releases built-up electricity through direct physical contact rather than normal electrical discharge.

species.name: Silvolt
species.description: Ancient carvings depict this Pokémon channeling lightning through martial arts techniques. Its unique fighting style allows it to overcome traditional electrical immunities through precise strikes.

species.name: Mounteen
species.description: Its crystalline horns have developed into impressive branching structures that glow faintly in moonlight. Mounteen travel in small herds through highland passes, their hoofbeats creating rhythmic patterns that mountain folk use to predict weather changes. The minerals in their diet determine the color and properties of their horns.

species.name: Mountelder
species.description: Ancient guardians of mountain peaks, Mountelder are rarely seen below the snowline. Their massive crystalline horns are highly valuable. Legends tell of Mountelder that have lived for centuries, their horns growing so large that lost travelers mistake them for crystalline formations on mountainsides.

species.name: Horrish
species.description: They travel in small schools that can purify remarkable volumes of water, leaving cleansed patches in even the most contaminated environments. Ancient sailors believed Horrish appeared in waters that had been tainted by human sin, their ghostly forms representing departed spirits come to cleanse wrongdoing.

species.name: Jirachi
species.description: This ancient being exists simultaneously in the material world and the realm of dreams. Once every millennium, when specific stars align, Jirachi awakens fully for seven days. During this time, it can reshape reality according to the wishes of those it deems worthy.

species.name: Deoxys
species.description: An entity born when cosmic radiation from distant stars struck raw ether in the Void between planes. Deoxys constantly reconfigures its cellular structure, allowing it to adapt instantly to any environment or threat.

species.name: Protoxys
species.description: This enigmatic crystalline entity emerges from meteorites that have traversed the Void between planes. Within its translucent structure, complex DNA-like patterns continuously form and dissipate, suggesting a consciousness in the process of becoming.

species.name: Scyther
species.description: Believed to originate from beyond the Crown of Stars, somehow entering our world through planar disturbances. Their blades can slice through dimensional barriers, creating brief windows into other realities.

species.name: Razcor
species.description: It can perceive and interact with multiple realities simultaneously, making its movements appear unpredictable and impossible to counter. Ancient texts warn of looking directly into the cosmic void within its eyes, as some observers report experiencing visions of distant worlds or possible futures.

species.name: Mudow
species.description: Folklore warns against following the soft, purple glow of their eyes, as they may lead travelers deeper into the swamp where the veil between worlds grows thin.

species.name: Marshade
species.description: The purple rings on its body pulse with otherworldly energy during moonless nights. When threatened, they can partially phase into the shadow realm, making portions of their body intangible.

species.name: Swampadow
species.description: Many believe them to be merely legends used to frighten children away from dangerous swamps. Their massive forms shift between solid and spectral states.

species.name: Treecko
species.description: Folklore warns against following these Pokémon into hollow trees, as those who do may find themselves emerging decades later-if at all.

species.name: Grovyle
species.description: The leaf blades on its arms exist partially in the Depths of Twilight, allowing them to slice through both physical matter and spiritual energy.

species.name: Sceptile
species.description: The spectral grove growing from its back contains trees extinct for millennia. When it walks through the oldest forests, whispers can be heard from the trees-secrets and wisdom from an age long lost.

species.name: Torchick
species.description: Their silent presence is considered an ill omen. The black flames seem to pull heat away, leaving a strange, empty cold in its wake.

species.name: Combusken
species.description: These Pokémon can witness echoes of past destructions, moving through the footprints of ancient fires as if walking through memories.

species.name: Blaziken
species.description: When it fights at full power, shadows of past destruction overlap with reality, as if all fires throughout history were burning simultaneously.

species.name: Smudgel
species.description: Smudgel are commonly found in urban areas across the Shiman Federation, particularly in cities. These diligent Pokémon have developed a unique relationship with human society, serving as invaluable assistants in maintenance and cleaning work. Unlike their artistic cousin Smeargle, Smudgel's tail secretes a special cleaning solution that can break down most common stains and grime.

species.name: Squeagle
species.description: Sqeagle are highly valued in the Shiman Federation's industrial sectors and are often found supervising teams of Smudgel in large facilities. Their bodies have developed a metallic sheen, with portions of their fur becoming steel-like bristles that can scrub away even the most stubborn industrial grime.

species.name: Vespot
species.description: Vespot is distinguished from other Vespair by its darkened chitin and enlarged stinger, saturated with concentrated venom. It is rarely seen far from the colony's inner chambers, where it serves as the last line of defence against intruders.

species.name: Vespina
species.description: Vespina's abdomen glows faintly gold from the Royal Jelly stored within it, and the colony is instinctively drawn to this light. It seldom moves from the heart of the hive, directing the colony through pheromones alone.
